cards.title: List customer names
cards.explanation: Choose explicit columns and stable output names. All shared SQL cards run on the seeded SQLite and PostgreSQL playgrounds.

cards.title: Find paid orders over a threshold
cards.explanation: Filter before aggregation. Numeric amounts use integer units in this fixture to avoid floating-point rounding.

cards.title: Find the two largest orders
cards.explanation: The id tie breaker makes the limited result deterministic.

cards.title: Join customers to their orders
cards.code:
SELECT c.name, o.id, o.total
FROM customers AS c
JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
ORDER BY o.id;
cards.explanation: Each order becomes one result row with its customer name.

cards.title: Find customers without orders
cards.code:
SELECT c.id, c.name
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.id IS NULL
ORDER BY c.id;
cards.explanation: The missing non-null primary key identifies customers with no matching order.

cards.title: Group paid totals per customer
cards.code:
SELECT customer_id, SUM(total) AS paid_total
FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid'
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING SUM(total) >= 50
ORDER BY customer_id;
cards.explanation: Aggregate only paid orders and keep customers reaching the threshold.

cards.title: Find customers with no email
cards.explanation: NULL represents an absent value. It differs from an empty string. Default NULL sort position differs between SQLite and PostgreSQL.

cards.title: Find customers with a paid order
cards.explanation: EXISTS returns each customer once even when several paid orders match.

cards.title: Name customer totals before filtering
cards.explanation: Use a CTE to separate aggregation from the final report.

cards.title: Rank orders within each customer
cards.explanation: Number each customer’s orders from largest to smallest with a stable tie breaker.

cards.title: Add a customer with a supplied key
cards.code:
INSERT INTO customers (id, name, email)
VALUES (5, 'Eve', 'eve@example.test');
cards.explanation: Shared examples supply ids explicitly: generated-key syntax differs between SQLite and PostgreSQL.

cards.title: Mark one order as paid
cards.code:
UPDATE orders SET status = 'paid'
WHERE id = 2 AND status = 'pending';
cards.explanation: The key and current-state predicate prevent changing unrelated orders.

cards.title: Delete one cancelled order
cards.code:
DELETE FROM orders
WHERE id = 4 AND status = 'cancelled';
cards.explanation: Delete only the known cancelled order; the seeded customer remains.

cards.title: Enforce unique inventory codes
cards.explanation: Duplicate codes, missing codes and negative quantities are rejected by both engines.

cards.title: Index customer order lookups
cards.code:
CREATE INDEX orders_customer_total
ON orders (customer_id, total);
cards.explanation: This index supports filtering orders by customer and then by total. Plans are engine-specific.

cards.title: Roll back a trial price change
cards.explanation: The trial update is discarded. The database tests also provoke a constraint error and recover through a savepoint on both engines.

cards.title: Bind a customer lookup value (SQLite)
cards.code:
-- SQLite only
SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id = ?;
cards.explanation: SQLite only. Bind [1] through the SQLite API. The Python sqlite3 companion uses this exact convention. Use the PostgreSQL variant after changing the dialect.

cards.title: Enable SQLite foreign-key enforcement
cards.code:
-- SQLite only
PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
cards.explanation: SQLite only. This is connection-local and must run outside an active transaction.

cards.title: Return a generated PostgreSQL key
cards.explanation: PostgreSQL only. No SQLite rowid assumptions are used.

cards.title: Update a customer on a key conflict
cards.code:
-- PostgreSQL only
INSERT INTO customers (id, name, email)
VALUES (1, 'Ada Lovelace', 'ada@example.test')
ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name
RETURNING id, name;
cards.explanation: PostgreSQL only. The existing email remains unchanged because only name is assigned.

cards.title: Read a PostgreSQL JSON property
cards.code:
-- PostgreSQL only
SELECT payload->>'name' AS name
FROM (VALUES ('{"name":"Ada","active":true}'::jsonb)) AS data(payload)
WHERE payload @> '{"active":true}'::jsonb;
cards.explanation: PostgreSQL only. Filter JSON documents using containment before extracting a property.

cards.title: Bind a customer lookup value (PostgreSQL)
cards.code:
-- PostgreSQL only
SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id = $1;
cards.explanation: PostgreSQL only. Pass [1] as the values array to node-postgres, or pass 1 to Go QueryRowContext. Values never become SQL syntax.
